title: In-session subagent rules per role (Claude and Codex)
goal: Every pipeline session gets a short, role-specific rule for in-session subagents (Claude Agent tool, Codex multi_agent): read-only scouts only, bounded fan-out, models inside pipeline.models.scope, reviewer subagents of the reviewer's own model, no subagents in QA; parallel writes stay subtasks dispatched with --phase implement. Data in the registry, one policy copy in delivery.md, rule lines in every dispatch prompt, a read-only factory-explorer plugin agent, and a doctor check of the Codex subagent model.

tasks.grade_reason: dispatch output change plus a config-hash test; same files as prompts
tasks.objective: Task worktrees made by `dispatch --phase lead` show as top-level worktrees in Orca, without their lead/child lineage, because the dispatch creates them with `git worktree add --no-track` (on purpose: `orca worktree create` writes branch.<name>.base into the shared .git/config). Fix: after the `git worktree add` line, `dispatch --phase lead` prints `orca worktree set --worktree path:<task worktree> --parent-worktree path:<integration checkout of plan.topic>` (the checkout that has the plan topic, else the repo checkout); verified by hand on 2026-11-09 that `orca worktree set` writes only Orca metadata (the .git/config hash was unchanged). When the run lead creates the integration checkout itself, delivery.md names the same `orca worktree set --parent-worktree path:<main checkout>` step. A no-worktree repo prints nothing new. Record the lesson where it belongs: delivery.md section 4 next to the existing `orca worktree create` lesson (lineage through `orca worktree set`, never through `orca worktree create`), and a one-line Operating lessons entry in .claude/CLAUDE.md with its reason. Tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh: the lead handoff prints the set line with the right parent, nothing new for a no-worktree repo, and the printed commands never include `orca worktree create`. Changelog fragment changelog.d/orca-lineage.md (### Fixed). Also (explorer-agent review finding): tests/affected.py does not map agents/* to tests/skills-lint.sh, so run-all --affected and suite reuse skip the agent lint when only an agent file changes; add agents/* to the skills-lint.sh extra inputs, with a case in the affected tests if one exists. Also (seen 2026-11-10): `orca worktree rm` on a task worktree made by `git worktree add` deletes the directory but can leave a prunable git worktree record, so `git branch -d` of the task branch fails ('used by worktree'). The cleanup commands `cleanup` prints for a plain git task worktree use `git worktree remove <path>` (no --force), or follow `orca worktree rm` with `git worktree prune`; record that in delivery.md section 8 item 1 and test the printed cleanup commands. Also (doctor-codex finding): README.md doctor row lists the dev-tool states OK / DOWN / MISSING without the new WARN state; add it. Also (seen 2026-11-10, user asked to fix): after the registry task was integrated, `orca worktree rm` left an empty task directory that Windows reports busy ('being used by another process') and an Orca worktree record shown as 'Delete failed'; git had already pruned the worktree and the branch was deleted. A released session whose CLI never exited (a Codex CLI started for a session that was stopped when codex went down) is the likely holder. Fix: (1) before removing a task worktree, the run lead and `cleanup` check that no live session or process still uses it: the task lead's Orca Run has no unreleased worker, no Orca terminal is bound to the worktree, and the task lead confirms each released worker's CLI exited (a released Codex worker: its codex process is gone); (2) `cleanup` reports a leftover directory (empty or not) or an Orca record of a removed worktree as LEFTOVER with the exact commands (`git worktree prune`, then `orca worktree rm --worktree path:<dir>` once the directory is free), never CLEAN; (3) never kill a process the run did not start: name it (PID, command) and leave the decision to the user. Record this in delivery.md section 8 (items 1 and 3, and 'Releasing a session does not stop its test processes'), with tests for the cleanup output (leftover directory, stale Orca record, busy directory reported, no kill). Note (2026-11-10): main (PR #89, commit 464d2da) already prints `orca worktree set` for new task worktrees and records the Orca visibility lesson; after main-sync merge plugin-subagent-rules into this task branch, keep main's lineage code and drop any duplicate, and keep only what main lacks (cleanup leftover and prune rules, README WARN, agents/* in affected). Also two gate bugs seen 2026-11-10 after main-sync merged origin/main into the topic: (a) `gate` marks the reviews of registry, policy, explorer-agent and doctor-codex STALE ('owned paths changed after <sha>': AGENTS.md, skills/factory-core/SKILL.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, tests/skills-lint.sh, registry.json, ...) although `git diff <reviewed sha> HEAD -- <those paths>` is empty: uncovered_changes (scripts/factory-pipeline.py, used at the review STALE check near the end of cmd_gate) must ignore a path whose content at HEAD equals its content at the reviewed commit, and must not count commits that arrived through a merge of the repo's default branch (origin/main); (b) `gate` lists the plan file itself (docs/plans/<plan>.json) as 'changes outside every task's owned paths': the plan file and docs/plans/<plan>/report.md belong to the run lead and are never stray. Tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh for both (a merge of the default branch after reviews keeps them current; a real later change to an owned path still makes the review STALE).

tasks.grade_reason: gate attribution logic over merge graphs; a wrong rule hides real post-review edits
tasks.objective: Gate follow-up (seen on this plan after orca-lineage merged, gate at a8535b6): reviews of registry (tests/run-all.sh) and policy (docs/codex.md, skills/delivery/SKILL.md, skills/factory-core/references/parallel-work.md, tests/orca-commands.test.sh, tests/parallel-policy.test.sh) are still STALE. Those files changed only through task main-sync, which merged origin/main INSIDE its task branch (f2ddb21) and was then merged into the topic with --no-ff (fcbbe1c): the pipeline's own prescribed way. _uncovered_changes in scripts/factory-pipeline.py recognises a default-branch merge only on the topic's first-parent chain, so this nested one is not exempt, and main-sync's review does not cover the earlier tasks' paths either. Fix: (1) a default-branch merge reached through a task merge (any merge commit between the reviewed sha and target whose other parent is the default branch tip or contains it) is exempt the same way: its side commits are nobody's task work, only its conflict resolutions count; and (2) those conflict resolutions are covered by the merging task's current PASS review when that task depends on the earlier task (main-sync depends on registry and policy). A real post-review edit on the topic or in a task branch outside such a merge stays STALE. Tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh: nested default-branch merge keeps earlier reviews current; its conflict resolution is covered by the merging task's review and STALE without it; a direct post-review edit is still STALE. Verify on this plan: gate shows no STALE. Changelog fragment changelog.d/gate-nested-merge.md (### Fixed).
